verses.text: Send lambs as a gift to the ruler of the land, from Sela across the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
Like birds that have been chased away, like a nest that has been scattered, so are the women of Moab at the crossings of the Arnon River.
"Give us advice! Make a fair decision! Cover us with your shade like night in the middle of the day! Hide those who have been driven out! Do not betray those who are running for their lives!

Let the people driven out of Moab stay with you. Be a hiding place for them from the destroyer." For the one who treats people cruelly will come to an end. Destruction will stop. The attacker will disappear from the land.
Then a throne will be set up in faithful love. Someone from the family of David will sit on it in faithfulness. He will judge fairly, seek justice, and be quick to do what is right.
We have heard about Moab's pride, how very proud it is. We have heard of its arrogance, its pride, and its anger. But its boasting is empty.
So the people of Moab will cry. Everyone will cry for Moab. You will mourn and be heartbroken for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth.

The fields of Heshbon are dying, and so are the vines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its best vines, which once reached as far as Jazer and spread out into the wilderness. Its branches spread out and went across the sea.
So I weep, as Jazer weeps, for the vines of Sibmah. I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh. For the shouts of battle have fallen on your summer fruit and your harvest.
Happiness and joy are taken away from the fruitful fields. No one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one stomps grapes in the winepresses. I have put an end to the shouting.
So my heart cries for Moab like the sad music of a harp, and my inner being aches for Kir Hareseth.
When Moab goes to its high place and wears itself out, when it goes to its temple to pray, it will do no good.
This is the message the LORD spoke about Moab in the past.

But now the LORD says, "Within three years, counted exactly as a hired worker counts the years, Moab's glory will be brought down, along with all its many people. Only a few will be left, and they will be weak."
